verdict.rationale: Babylon.js is open-source (Apache-2.0) and supports open, standard 3D file formats like glTF, OBJ, and STL alongside its own .babylon format, so scene/asset data isn't locked into a single proprietary format and can be exported or moved elsewhere. However, there is no first-party or community evidence of a comprehensive 'export all my data and leave' workflow, no discussion of data portability/lock-in avoidance as a stated goal, and no independent confirmation that full round-trip export preserves all engine-specific features (physics, materials, animations). missing for 10: explicit data-export/migration documentation, independent verification of full-fidelity export to open formats, and any framing of this as an intentional anti-lock-in feature.
